skill.name: image-to-video
skill.description: Routes still-image animation requests to HappyHorse, Wan, or Seedance models through the RunComfy CLI. It provides model-specific prompts for general animation, voiceover lip-sync, and multimodal reference workflows.
skill.summary: Route still-image animation requests to a suitable RunComfy video model.
skill.author: skills-collective

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and standard configuration paths. Eight findings confirm intended installation or execution of external CLI commands. The skill also sends prompts and user media references to a third-party model service.

remediation.issue: The workflow installs and executes a third-party CLI package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version, publish integrity verification steps, and require user confirmation before installation or first execution.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media references are processed by RunComfy and its model infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain explicit consent, link the applicable privacy and retention policies, and warn users against submitting sensitive or unauthorized media.

remediation.issue: User-derived prompts and URLs may become shell command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured process arguments or standard input, validate media URLs, and never interpolate user content into a shell command string.

content.user_title: Animate Still Images with the Right RunComfy Model
content.value_statement: Choosing an image-to-video model can waste time and credits. This skill routes each request to a suitable RunComfy model and provides focused prompting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes portrait, product, and general animation requests to HappyHorse 1.0 I2V.
Routes custom voiceover lip-sync requests to Wan 2.7 with an audio URL.
Routes combined image, video, and audio reference workflows to Seedance 2.0 Pro.
Provides model-specific duration, resolution, aspect ratio, seed, and media input guidance.
Builds motion-focused prompts and invokes the selected model through the RunComfy CLI.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and accessible source media URLs.
Selects one model per call and does not blend routes or stitch separate clips.
Clips are limited to each model's supported duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and media sizes.
Prompts and media references are processed by third-party RunComfy infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Create Portrait Motion
use_cases.description: Animate a portrait with controlled facial movement, stable identity, and a simple camera move for short social videos.

use_cases.title: Build Product Reveals
use_cases.description: Turn a product image into a short reveal with preserved packaging, smooth camera motion, and deliberate lighting changes.

use_cases.title: Produce Localized Spokesperson Clips
use_cases.description: Create lip-synced variants by reusing a visual direction and changing the voiceover URL for each language.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Portrait
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this portrait from [image URL] with subtle breathing, blinking, and gentle camera drift. Create a five-second vertical clip with stable facial features.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Product Reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate [product image URL] with a slow orbit and rising rim light. Keep the packaging, logo, proportions, and background geometry unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-Sync a Voiceover
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a vertical spokesperson clip using [audio URL]. Match the duration to the voiceover, keep the camera locked, and avoid subtitles or flicker.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Multimodal References
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [image URL] for the subject, [video URL] for scene motion, and [audio URL] for voice tone. Create an eight-second coordinated clip.

output_examples.input: Animate this portrait with subtle movement for a vertical profile video.
output_examples.output: Selected HappyHorse 1.0 I2V. Planned a five-second vertical clip with blinking, breathing, stable facial features, and gentle camera drift.

output_examples.input: Turn this package photo into a clean rotating product reveal.
output_examples.output: Selected HappyHorse 1.0 I2V. Planned one slow orbit with unchanged packaging, stable background geometry, and gradually intensifying rim light.

output_examples.input: Create a twelve-second spokesperson video synchronized to my voiceover.
output_examples.output: Selected Wan 2.7. Planned a locked medium close-up, twelve-second duration, custom voiceover lip-sync, and controls against subtitles and flicker.

best_practices: Lead with one clear motion or camera action and describe only what should change.
State preservation requirements for faces, products, logos, costumes, and background geometry.
Match duration to reference audio and reuse seeds when comparing controlled variants.
anti_patterns: Do not combine several competing camera moves or character actions in one short clip.
Do not restate every visible detail when motion, lighting, and preservation instructions are more useful.
Do not submit sensitive, unlicensed, or inaccessible media URLs to third-party model services.

faq.question: Which model is selected by default?
faq.answer: HappyHorse 1.0 I2V is the default for general portrait, product, and still-image animation requests.

faq.question: Can I use my own voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill routes custom voiceover lip-sync requests to Wan 2.7 using an accessible MP3 or WAV URL.

faq.question: Can one request combine image, video, and audio references?
faq.answer: Yes. Seedance 2.0 Pro supports combined image, video, and audio references within its documented limits.

faq.question: Does the skill create long videos?
faq.answer: No. The documented routes produce short clips with maximum durations of about fifteen seconds.

faq.question: Does it require a local installation?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires the RunComfy CLI, account authentication, and network access to RunComfy services.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated outputs into the output directory selected for the request.
